source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Macroeconomics, Ch. 2 (National Income Accounting).

sections.heading: 1. Circular Flow and Key Aggregates
points: The **circular flow of income** shows the flow of money/goods between households and firms (factor payments and spending).
Three methods of measuring national income: **Product (value-added), Income, and Expenditure** methods — all give the same total.
**Final goods** (counted) vs **intermediate goods** (not counted, to avoid double counting).

sections.heading: 2. Key Concepts
points: **GDP (Gross Domestic Product)** = value of all final goods/services produced **within a country** in a year.
**GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad (NFIA)**.
**NDP = GDP − depreciation**; **NNP = GNP − depreciation**.
**National Income (NNP at factor cost)** = NNP at market price − net indirect taxes.

sections.heading: 3. Market Price vs Factor Cost; Nominal vs Real
points: **Market price** includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies; **factor cost** = market price − net indirect taxes (indirect taxes − subsidies).
**Nominal GDP** = at current prices; **Real GDP** = at constant (base-year) prices (removes inflation).
**GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100** — measures the price level.

sections.heading: 4. Uses and Limitations of GDP
points: **Uses:** GDP measures the size/growth of an economy, and (per capita GDP) living standards.

points.text: **Limitations of GDP as a welfare measure:**
sub: Excludes **non-market/household work** and the informal economy.
Ignores **negative externalities** (pollution) and quality of life.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Three methods: product (value added), income, expenditure.
GDP = within country; GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad.
NNP at factor cost = National Income; factor cost = market price − net indirect taxes.
Real GDP (constant prices) removes inflation; GDP deflator = (Nominal/Real)×100.
GDP ignores distribution, non-market work, externalities.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **GDP = within a country**; **GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad**.
**Real GDP is at constant (base-year) prices** (removes inflation).
**Factor cost = market price − net indirect taxes** (indirect taxes − subsidies).
GDP is **not** a full measure of welfare (ignores inequality, externalities, non-market work).
